title: Smile and Well
premise: When Elodie Halloran returns to the coastal town of Well to bury her twin sister Odile, she insists the drowned woman in the coffin is a stranger—the town's founders' ritual demands a twin, and everyone, including her grieving mother, seems to accept the swap too easily. Digging through Odile's belongings, Elodie finds sleep recordings in which a second voice answers questions no one asked aloud, a voice that knows things only Odile could know—and knows Elodie's secrets too. As she uncovers the founders' covenant, which binds the town's prosperity to a twin's sacrifice every seventy years, Elodie realizes her own survival depended on Odile taking her place, and that the ritual is unfinished. In the flooded chapel beneath the old well, Elodie must choose: complete the rite and become the town's keeper, or break it and let Well drown with everything it has hidden—including the truth of which sister actually came home.
about_author: Tamsin Underhill is a former archivist from the Maine coast who spent a decade cataloguing the private papers of vanished seafaring families. She writes horror about towns that remember more than the people who live in them.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sister
chapters.summary: Elodie arrives in Well for the funeral, insisting the body is not Odile—yet the town, even her mother, gently corrects her. Third-person limited POV follows Elodie through the wake, where every mourner watches her a beat too long. Emotional beat: grief curdling into alienation, the reader unsure whether Elodie is in denial or the town is lying.

chapters.title: Odile's Room, Unchanged
chapters.summary: Elodie stays in her sister's preserved bedroom and finds a dictaphone and a box of sleep recordings labeled in Odile's handwriting. First-person Elodie POV. On the first tape, a voice that isn't Odile's answers questions Odile never asks. Emotional beat: the first crack in Elodie's certainty—dread replacing denial.

chapters.title: Questions in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie plays the tapes through the night; the second voice grows more fluent, addressing her by name though the recordings predate her return. Third-person POV, alternating with tape transcripts. The voice reveals a detail only Elodie knows: what she did the summer the sisters stopped speaking. Emotional beat: exposure—being seen by something that shouldn't see.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the town archive, Elodie finds the founders' covenant: Well prospers so long as a twin is given to the well-water every seventy years, and the survivor becomes the town's memory-keeper. Third-person POV with archive excerpts. Emotional beat: the horror of inherited bargains—her whole childhood re-read as preparation.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Water
chapters.summary: Elodie confronts her mother, who admits the swap was real: Odile drowned in Elodie's place, and the town agreed to let Elodie believe otherwise. First-person Elodie POV. Her mother's loyalty is absolute, her guilt unspeakable. Emotional beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth made flesh—love that requires a lie.

chapters.title: The Second Voice Names Itself
chapters.summary: The voice on the tapes reveals it is the previous sacrifice—Odile's and Elodie's great-aunt—still answering questions in the dark beneath the chapel, and it warns that the rite is incomplete because the wrong twin was given willingly by another, not offered by herself. Third-person POV. Emotional beat: pity and terror braided together; the voice is victim and lure.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Odile's body disappears from the grave; things washed by the tide appear on doorsteps, each a keepsake from a past sacrifice. The town turns on Elodie, blaming her refusal to believe for the breach. Third-person POV, escalating communal menace. Emotional beat: siege—Elodie's invisibility revoked, the town's kindness revealed as surveillance.

chapters.title: Down the Well Shaft
chapters.summary: Guided by the voice and Odile's final tape, Elodie descends into the flooded chapel beneath the well, where the unfinished ritual waits: an offered twin must finish it or the covenant breaks and Well drowns. First-person Elodie POV, claustrophobic and dreamlike. Emotional beat: the point of no return; she finally chooses to believe.

chapters.title: The Offering
chapters.summary: In the chapel, Elodie finds Odile—alive in some sense, kept as the ritual's unfinished half—and learns the truth: Odile offered herself to save Elodie, but the rite requires the surviving twin's free consent. The voice and the town press her to consent and become keeper. Third-person POV at maximum pressure. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth—every option costs a life or a lie.

chapters.title: Smile and Well
chapters.summary: Elodie breaks the covenant instead, releasing the sacrificed voices and letting the sea reclaim the founders' bargain; she carries Odile's body out as Well floods behind them. In the epilogue, Elodie buries her sister under her own name and records one last tape, answering questions no one asks. First-person POV. Emotional beat: costly resolution—truth survived, but at the price of home, and the tapes keep whispering.
